rubric_hint.rule: 2 eligible species recorded beyond 250 m but within 1000 m, none within 250 m
rubric_hint.basis: prompts/rubric.md v1 applied to all rings 0-1000 m and effort; a default, not a verdict

reasons.claim: The notification is a 1.19 ha regeneration felling (Föryngringsavverkning) in Flen, status 'notified'. Completed felling overlaps 8.2% of the polygon (a 2002 felling), so this is not ALREADY_FELLED.
No eligible species within 250 m. The only red-listed record there is Scorzonera humilis (NT, 60 m, 2021, unc 25 m). The tool marks it not felling-relevant, so it is not eligible.

Two eligible species are recorded beyond 250 m but within 1000 m. Pannaria conoplea (EN lichen, 968 m, 2018, unc 100 m) has felling-relevant factors: lack of continuity forest and of large or old trees, changed stand structure and changed tree-species composition. Otidea concinna (VU fungus, 901 m and 968 m, 2024) has soil disturbance in forestry and changed stand structure as factors. This matches the rubric MEDIUM rule.

Effort within 1000 m is adequate: 2861 records, 92nd percentile, against a county median of 724. Near-site recording is thin: 2 records on 2 days within 250 m against a county median of 12, and none inside the polygon.

uncertainties: Both eligible species lie 900 m or more away, at the edge of the 1000 m ring. The polygon's equivalent radius is only 61 m, so they may say little about the stand.
The Pannaria conoplea record is from 2018 with 100 m uncertainty. Its present status is unknown.
Within 250 m there are few records (2). The near-site effort is below the county median of 12, so the absence of eligible species close by is weak evidence.
not_established: Whether any red-listed species occurs on the polygon.
Forest character or stand age: the tools do not state it.
Whether felling is legal or harmful.
Absence of species on or next to the site, including sensitive species hidden in public data.
next_action: A reviewer should judge whether habitat on the polygon is comparable to that around the records at about 900–970 m (GBIF links in E-29524 and E-29527). A short field or aerial-image check of the stand is warranted because near-site recording is sparse.
